findings.title: Redaction misses fan-out errors and response metadata
findings.invariant: Every response path must honor configured redaction, including errors, metadata, JSON keys and progress.
findings.impact: Synthetic credentials escaped in text and structured output; real sensitive diagnostics could cross the configured egress boundary. Scope is a local stdio client, not an unauthenticated network service.
findings.recommendation: Scrub the complete response and progress boundary, including keys with collision preservation; redact before truncation.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline core harness observed all three metadata/error leak cases; candidate tests cover full serialized responses. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Raw exception messages become successful fan-out return values.
Per-leg errors bypass the single-error scrub at lines 414–419.
Child-controlled denial names enter metadata.

preconditions: Redaction enabled; a provider diagnostic, denial field or structured key contains a credential-shaped value.
failure_sequence: A failing leg returns its raw diagnostic.
Fan-out or metadata rendering bypasses the single-error redactor.
The client receives the sensitive value.
counterevidence: Single successful output and single thrown errors were scrubbed, but those paths do not cover returned leg failures, metadata or JSON keys.
validation: Serialize partial/all-failed fan-out and structured/denied/progress cases; no synthetic marker survives, and colliding keys preserve every value.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Whole-agent replay is authorized by insufficient evidence
findings.invariant: A whole agent turn must not be repeated without proof that it was not dispatched or that its complete effects are safe to repeat.
findings.impact: Repeated execution was observed. Duplicate remote changes or charges are conditional on what the delegated agent did; no remote corruption or actual duplicate bill was demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Do not replay after dispatch. Let AGY handle native transient retries; record quota for later requests and invalidate stale discovery only for the next deliberate call.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline network/quota cases spawned twice; warm error spawned cold after delivery. Candidate regressions assert one dispatch. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Unchanged trees or unknown plan coverage permit a repeat.
Text-classified invalid model refreshes and dispatches again without admission proof.
Network failures repeat the entire request.

preconditions: A sent turn has file or external effects before a network, quota, invalid-model-like or uncertain warm failure.
failure_sequence: The first agent turn is dispatched.
A failure is classified using text or local tree state.
The bridge repeats a whole turn although neither condition proves external effects absent.
counterevidence: Tree fingerprints, write restrictions and denied actions constrain local behavior but cannot establish that no network or external process effect occurred. API-level retryability concerns a model request, not the entire agent workflow.
validation: Network/quota/model/uncertain-warm fake failures result in one dispatch even with an unchanged or unknown tree. Pre-send WarmUnavailable may fall back safely.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

locations.observation: Per-task prompt is added while original tasks remain.
The schema requires exactly one of prompt or tasks.

preconditions: A valid delegate_many call supplies tasks.
failure_sequence: The server creates task legs.
Each leg retains tasks and adds prompt.
Prompt building rejects both fields before the CLI starts.

validation: Two explicit tasks dispatch twice with one prompt per leg, including a custom-only inventory.

findings.title: Council selection loses explicit intent and pre-dispatch validation
findings.invariant: Fan-out must execute only the selected mode and validated distinct members, preserving caller versus automatic origin.
findings.impact: Unintended paid legs, duplicate votes, avoidable quota attempts, or rejected bridge-only selectors.

locations.observation: Singular model is ignored and default council selected.

Every leg-supplied model is treated as caller pinned.

findings.title: Failed attempts bypass accounting and later budget admission
findings.invariant: Admission must account for all observed failed work and must never equate missing usage with measured zero.
findings.impact: Reproduction spent 115 tokens under a 50-token admission limit; a 100-token warm failure was reported as only the 15-token cold retry.
findings.recommendation: Record all returned usage once, mark missing counters unknown, check immediately before each dispatch, and stop budgeted work when remaining spend is unknowable.
findings.verification_detail: Core harness contains networkBudget, quotaBudget and warmFailureAccounting observations. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Budget is checked per admitted logical call.
Only successful warm envelopes are recorded; timeout is emitted as zero usage.
A second dispatch follows failed spend without another budget check.

preconditions: Budget is configured; a failed first attempt spends tokens or a warm result reports usage before failing.
failure_sequence: The logical request passes admission.
Failure spends tokens; warm error usage is omitted or retry spend is recorded only after admission.
Another attempt dispatches or unknown usage looks free.
counterevidence: Concurrency admission already rechecks queued logical calls. This does not control secondary attempts, failed warm results or missing usage; no hard in-flight spending cap is claimed.
validation: Known failed spend blocks the next admission; uncertain outcomes increment unknownRuns and block a configured budget without claiming measured zero.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Warm launches omit request options and fail-open restricting flags
findings.invariant: Equivalent warm and cold requests must receive the same effective options and required restrictions.
findings.impact: Meaningful cold/warm behavior mismatch and potential execution with less restriction than configured.
findings.recommendation: Share effective permission/option requirements and include policy in reuse identity; fail closed for missing required flags.
findings.verification_detail: Execution harness observed warm roots [/repo] versus cold [/repo,/extra], slash commands disabled, and missing sandbox accepted warm but refused cold. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

preconditions: Warm sessions are enabled; requested roots/options differ or a streaming-capable CLI lacks requested --mode/--sandbox.
failure_sequence: Follow-up qualifies for warm execution.
Resident launch does not receive the same effective policy as cold execution.
Warm call succeeds with different roots, expansion or restrictions.
counterevidence: Warm already compares cwd and confinement roots; it does not compare every launch option. Public schemas do not expose every internal sandbox override, so the finding is limited to reachable configuration/options.
validation: Cold/warm option parity; zero delivery to incompatible or under-restricted residents; useful pre-dispatch errors.

findings.title: Cleanup can lose ownership of still-running descendants
findings.invariant: The bridge or relay must retain ownership of all spawned work until it is reaped or forcibly stopped.
findings.impact: Orphaned work can keep consuming tokens or touching the workspace after cancellation.
findings.recommendation: Track active and terminating ownership until confirmed exit or hard group cleanup; do not equate leader exit with descendant completion.
findings.verification_detail: Execution and relay harnesses observed surviving children; cold grandchild remained alive after 5638 ms. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Leader/pipe timeout resolves before the whole process group is gone.
Escalation can be cancelled on leader completion.
Dropped residents leave the registry, while shutdown clears their pending escalation.
Abort settles and cancels timers without equivalent descendant reap.

preconditions: A detached AGY child or descendant ignores SIGTERM, especially during cancel/timeout immediately followed by shutdown.
failure_sequence: Leader or resident is removed from active ownership.
Cleanup cancels escalation or exits.
A descendant continues after the bridge/relay reports termination.
counterevidence: Process groups and escalation already exist; their lifecycle is incomplete. Safe repros used disposable fake children and explicitly reaped survivors.
validation: Real fake descendant survives SIGTERM but is gone after cancellation; warm drop then shutdown sends SIGKILL; relay abort leaves no owned child.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: A stale warm resident survives an intervening cold continuation
findings.invariant: A conversation resident must not be reused after another process changes its history or execution policy.
findings.impact: Resident retention was reproduced. Stale model/history or presence-lock conflicts depend on live AGY behavior and are not asserted as proven provider corruption.
findings.recommendation: Invalidate and reap residents before cold continuation; refuse while a resident is actively busy.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline observed one resident, two warm turns, one cold turn and no kills before shutdown. Apply status: Resident invalidation and busy guards applied; local lifecycle tests passed. Live provider history/presence behavior remains a canary gap.

locations.observation: Explicit model/effort/write/schema routes cold without invalidating the resident.
Cold continuation can launch while prior resident still owns the conversation.
Later warm request reuses the retained process.

preconditions: A conversation alternates warm follow-up, a cold continuation with changed execution needs, then warm follow-up.
failure_sequence: First resident holds in-memory conversation state.
Cold continuation uses the same conversation independently.
Later warm request reuses the old resident.
counterevidence: Per-conversation admission serializes bridge work, but serial execution alone does not refresh another process history or release its presence lock.
validation: Warm→cold→warm changes resident identity and awaits exit; competing cold/ warm calls do not kill another active turn.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.impact: Failed or timed-out work is harder to assess or resume and can be mistaken for a generic failure with no useful result.

Caller loses useful partial text and conversation recovery details.

validation: Official-contract fixture with ERROR, exit3 and print_timeout retains partial/session, usage and incomplete status; interruption does not become success.

findings.impact: False confidence that no write occurred; this also amplified replay risk, counted separately by its execution invariant.
findings.recommendation: Propagate incomplete reasons, content-hash bounded relevant coverage and retain unknown instead of false-clean; never use local clean state to authorize whole-turn replay.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline error-return branch is static proof; candidate execution/worktree tests exercise inaccessible roots and watched coverage. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Unreadable directory returns the same sentinel as complete coverage.

Completion state does not accurately represent missing coverage.
Read-only/replay decisions can infer more than was observed.
counterevidence: Bounds and three-valued comparison already exist. The unreadable-directory branch fails to propagate the unknown state; filesystem observation never proves no remote effects.
validation: Inaccessible roots/subtrees and budget exhaustion yield unknown; ignored/nested changes are detected within stated coverage; require mode refuses unverifiable guarantees.

findings.title: Skill replacement removes the working installation before copying succeeds
findings.invariant: A failed skill replacement must preserve the prior working installation.
findings.impact: Local user skill edits or a working skill installation may be lost; replacement failure is not transactional.
findings.recommendation: Stage a full copy, preserve/rename the old destination, swap atomically where possible and roll back on failure; define collision behavior.

counterevidence: Symlink targets are skipped unless --force, but ordinary installed directories are still removed first. Top-level failure handling does not roll back.
validation: Injected staging/copy failure leaves prior skill bytes unchanged; successful replacement leaves no partial files; symlink policy preserved.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Cross-process cooldown updates can lose another writer’s entry
findings.invariant: Concurrent cooldown writers must preserve every active entry and the maximum same-model expiry.
findings.impact: A fresh client can forget a valid cooldown and spend another failed attempt discovering known quota exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Use independent immutable model/expiry records with maximum-expiry reads, or serialize the full read/merge/write operation.
findings.verification_detail: Interleaving is statically complete; candidate deterministic multi-process regression passes. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Read/merge/rename then verify is not one serialized transaction.
Whole-file atomic replace protects readers but not concurrent writers.

preconditions: Two bridge processes write different model cooldowns from the same old snapshot.
failure_sequence: Both read the old state.
Writer A saves and verifies its own entry.
Writer B later renames its snapshot and verifies, removing A’s entry.
counterevidence: Three bounded verification passes handle some interleavings but not this valid schedule; sequential tests cannot establish concurrent preservation.
validation: Overlapping independent writers preserve both models and the maximum same-model expiry for a fresh reader.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.invariant: Production installation must not require development-only packages omitted by that installation.
findings.impact: Supported deployment/installation path fails deterministically.
findings.recommendation: Skip the development-only hook in production and use reviewed lifecycle handling in Docker; smoke-test clean production install.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline production npm ci exited 127: husky not found. Candidate package smoke covers production shape. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Unconditional prepare invokes husky.
npm ci --omit=dev runs prepare without Husky installed.

preconditions: A production-only install is performed, including the documented Docker runtime stage.
failure_sequence: npm omits development dependencies.
Root prepare still invokes husky.
Install exits 127 before producing a usable runtime layer.
counterevidence: Development npm ci succeeds because Husky is present; that does not validate production-only installation.
validation: npm ci --omit=dev succeeds in an empty environment without Husky; packed stdio server starts and calls fake AGY on supported Node versions.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: The required aggregate CI job can be skipped instead of failing
findings.invariant: The required CI aggregate must explicitly fail when a required predecessor fails or is cancelled.
findings.impact: Required-status enforcement can be weaker than the project’s stated gate. Actual hosted rules were not independently inspected.
findings.recommendation: Always run the aggregate and explicitly require success for each relevant predecessor, including package and commitlint.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline YAML plus GitHub documented skip semantics establish the configuration defect conditional on the stated required check. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: needs:suite plus default success condition skips the aggregator after predecessor failure.

preconditions: The aggregate test status is required as the workflow comment states, and a matrix predecessor fails or is cancelled.
failure_sequence: Matrix job fails.
Aggregate job does not execute due to dependency success semantics.
Branch protection sees a skipped aggregate rather than an explicit failed required conclusion.
counterevidence: Matrix tests still fail visibly, but a required aggregate must not rely on that visibility alone; commitlint was not included in its required dependencies.
validation: Workflow graph includes required jobs; failure/cancellation propagates to failed aggregate; push versus PR skip rules are explicit.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Release manifests describe incompatible package versions
findings.invariant: Every distribution surface must identify the same tested release artifact.
findings.impact: Distribution identity is inconsistent; source test success does not prove the advertised installed artifact.
findings.recommendation: Align one candidate version and add a consistency gate plus packed-artifact handshake tests.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline exact version fields re-read; candidate check:release and package smoke pass. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Package advertises 3.1.0.
Lock root/package advertise 3.0.4.
MCP manifest directs users to 2.0.0.

preconditions: A consumer installs using the MCP registry manifest or release tooling reads these independent version fields.
failure_sequence: Package, lock and registry identify different versions.
Registry-selected artifact differs from the current source-tested package.
Users can receive older behavior while reading newer release claims.
counterevidence: Server handshake reads package.json, so handshake itself is not independently hardcoded; other manifests still diverge.
validation: Package, lock roots, MCP package and handshake all report 3.2.0; clean tarball install exercises the actual built entry.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Raw stream and log accumulation are not bounded by final output limits
findings.invariant: Every raw-output accumulator needs a defined bound and an explicit incomplete outcome on overflow.
findings.impact: Local bridge resource exhaustion or silent loss of stream context despite a configured answer cap. No production OOM was induced.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit bounded raw capture and log carry, fail incomplete on overflow, retain safe clipped recovery context, and scrub before intermediate clipping.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline growth paths are static proof; candidate bound regressions are included in specialist/full suites. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: streamedText grows independently of the stdout tail.
One read allocates the entire appended file delta and grows carry.
NDJSON carry and accumulated partial text lack explicit bounds.

preconditions: A long-running or malformed provider emits very large text, chunks or a line without a newline.
failure_sequence: Final-answer limit is applied after execution.
Raw/carry/stream buffers continue growing beforehand.
Process memory can grow without a corresponding admission bound or clear incomplete failure.
counterevidence: Cold stdout has a 64 MiB rolling tail and prompt size is bounded, but auxiliary accumulators and warm streams are separate.
validation: Controlled oversized cold/warm/log output fails with output_limit and preserved session/usage uncertainty; no silent truncated success.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: MCP progress is not monotonic across warm updates or fan-out legs
findings.invariant: Progress values must increase for each MCP request progress token.
findings.impact: Clients can display stalled/regressing progress or reject protocol-invalid updates.
findings.recommendation: Use a server-owned increasing sequence per request token, retaining provider type/text only as scrubbed descriptive metadata.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline values are directly traceable; candidate warm regression observes [1,2]. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Provider stepIndex is forwarded as request progress.
Every warm update uses stepIndex zero.

preconditions: Client requests progress for a warm call or a multi-leg request whose provider indices restart.
failure_sequence: Provider emits repeated/reset step indices.
Server forwards them with one progress token.
Progress does not increase as the MCP contract requires.
counterevidence: One-second throttling reduces notification volume but does not create monotonic values.
validation: Repeated warm index zero produces progress 1 then 2; fan-out resets do not decrease the token’s progress.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Intermediate quota logs prematurely terminate native AGY retry recovery
findings.invariant: An intermediate retryable provider log must not override a later successful native agent result.
findings.impact: Unnecessary failure and lost native continuity. This is distinct from duplicate whole-turn execution, tracked in AUD-002.
findings.recommendation: Let AGY own transient recovery; classify terminal envelope/status/exit first; use logs only as compatible terminal evidence and record cooldown for later work.
findings.verification_detail: Baseline poller explicitly terminates on any match; current changelog documents native transient retries preserving tool output. Candidate runner tests cover success after a 429 log. Apply status: Applied in candidate 3.2.0; focused and final Linux integration checks passed.

locations.observation: Any appended quota-looking log immediately kills the child.
Historical log signal is treated as quota regardless of later success.

preconditions: Current AGY internally retries a transient 429/capacity error and can later complete the same agent turn.
failure_sequence: An intermediate quota-looking log appears.
Bridge kills AGY before its native recovery completes, or treats historical log as terminal.
A recoverable turn becomes failed and may enter unsafe wrapper replay in the baseline.
counterevidence: Log quota detection supports older CLIs, but a log line alone cannot distinguish transient intermediate capacity from terminal model exhaustion.
validation: A success envelope following a transient 429 succeeds once; terminal exhausted result fails once and records cooldown.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing architecture; no new service or provider framework is required.

findings.title: Evaluate new family defaults with representative work before promotion
findings.invariant: Automatic routing changes should follow measured task and cost outcomes rather than family naming or price-table inference.
findings.impact: Potential better task outcomes and resource use, but no measured savings or speedup is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Keep existing defaults; canary explicit models with an approved budget, then compare acceptance success, latency, tokens/credits and quota failure per tool.
findings.verification_detail: No paid model benchmark was performed. Candidate preserves automatic defaults and documents evaluation choices. Apply status: Deferred deliberately. Selection support shipped in candidate; automatic policy changes await approved account-specific evaluation.

locations.observation: Automatic Flash/Pro policy is an existing default, not a measured Gemini 4 comparison.
Council membership adds independent paid turns.

preconditions: Operator wants to change automatic defaults or expand council membership after enabling Gemini 4 selection.
failure_sequence: Family support is added from account discovery.
A global new default would alter quality, latency, entitlement and spend assumptions.
A frozen comparative workload can establish whether a per-tool promotion is justified.
counterevidence: Current inventory proves selection availability only; direct API price tables do not establish subscription credits or AGY total cost. Historical Flash benchmarks cannot be relabeled.
validation: All selected variants remain usable now; promote a default only with noninferior task acceptance and measured operational benefit on the agreed workload.
tradeoffs: Adds bounded evaluation effort but avoids an unmeasured global behavior and spend change.
